newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem sees zero inflation in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem sees zero inflation in 1997.

text.p: Argentine consumer prices declined in December, bringing the year's inflation tally to 0.1 percent, and prices will remain flat next year, President Carlos Menem said in comments reported Tuesday.
Menem was quoted by local newspapers as saying prices in December eased 0.3 percent, compared to a drop of 0.2 percent in November and an uptick of 0.1 percent in December 1995.
"I don't remember any other period with six years of stability," said Menem, refering to the convertibility plan launched in April 1991, which tamed runaway inflation.
Inflation fell to 84 percent in 1991 from 1,343 percent in 1990 and 4,923 percent in 1989.
